common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Carpal tunnel syndrome (median nerve compression).

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (median nerve compression). right wrist pain, hand numbness, and weak grip waking him up at night for 3 months. 45M reports 3 months of burning pain and numbness in the thumb, index, and middle fingers of his right hand. Wakes up at night needing to shake his hand to get relief. Grip strength has become slightly weak.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (median nerve compression).
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (median nerve compression).
reference_soap.plan: Confirm the distribution and examine sensation, thumb abduction/opposition, and thenar bulk while considering cervical radiculopathy or another neuropathy. Start a neutral-position nighttime splint and address modifiable contributors. Obtain electrodiagnostic testing when the diagnosis is uncertain, symptoms are persistent/severe, or results would guide intervention; arrange prompt hand-specialist assessment for progressive weakness, thenar atrophy, or persistent sensory loss.
